description: MongoDB 8 health metric catalog. Derived from dbi services scoring framework v0.30+. Adapted for document database architecture.
release_notes: v1.2.1 (2026-09-23): catalog maturity label added (draft: not yet reviewed by a technology leader, neither for collection nor for scoring). No metric, threshold, weight or rule change. v1.2.0: schema-ready for consistency_rules (rules deferred to Technology Leader work). v1.1.0: Subcategory point allocations within Capacity, Performance, and Future-Proofing pillars differ from the architecture specification (SCORING_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.3). These splits have been stable since v1.0.0 and are flagged for tech-leader review. See docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md for details.

metrics.description: Length of replication history retained in the oplog. A short window risks forcing full resyncs after secondaries fall behind.
metrics.remediation: Increase oplog size: rs.printReplicationInfo() to check; set oplogSizeMB in mongod.conf or replSetResizeOplog command

metrics.description: Whether oplog size (replication.oplogSizeMB) is explicit. Relying on the 5%-of-disk default leaves the oplog window unpredictable.
metrics.remediation: Set replication.oplogSizeMB in mongod.conf based on replication lag and write volume

metrics.description: Continuity of the oplog. Gaps or holes break secondary sync and force a full initial resync.
metrics.remediation: Investigate via rs.printReplicationInfo(); consider increasing oplog size to prevent truncation under heavy writes

metrics.description: Whether oplog replay can deliver point-in-time recovery within RPO. Requires oplog window to span the gap between backups.
metrics.remediation: Ensure oplog window exceeds RPO target; document oplog-based PITR procedure

metrics.description: Atlas continuous-backup oplog retention. Determines the PITR window available from Cloud Backup.
metrics.remediation: Configure oplog retention hours in Atlas continuous backup settings

metrics.description: Cadence of recurring backups (mongodump, Atlas, or PBM). Required to bound data loss to the schedule interval.
metrics.remediation: Implement and document a backup schedule (daily minimum); prefer PBM or Atlas for production

metrics.description: Time elapsed since the last successful backup. Excessive age means a stale recovery point and growing data-loss exposure.
metrics.remediation: Verify backup jobs are completing successfully; check PBM status or Atlas backup history

metrics.description: Whether Atlas Cloud Backup (continuous or snapshot) is on. Required for managed PITR and snapshot recovery on Atlas.
metrics.remediation: Enable Cloud Backup in Atlas cluster settings; configure snapshot frequency and retention

metrics.description: Periodic restore-test verification of backup integrity (mongorestore drill). Without it, restore failures are discovered at the worst possible time.
metrics.remediation: Schedule periodic restore tests to validate backup integrity

metrics.description: Use of Percona Backup for MongoDB (PBM). Recommended for consistent self-managed replica/sharded cluster backups with PITR.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Percona Backup for MongoDB for consistent physical backups with PITR support

metrics.description: Whether point-in-time recovery is available (PBM PITR or Atlas continuous backup). Without it, recovery snaps to the last full backup.
metrics.remediation: Enable PITR in PBM (pitr.enabled: true in pbm config) or Atlas continuous backup

metrics.description: Encryption at rest for backup artifacts. Required where backup media may travel offsite or compliance demands it.
metrics.remediation: Use PBM with encrypted storage or Atlas Cloud Backup (encrypted by default)

metrics.description: Use of mongodump --oplog on replica sets. Required for a consistent point-in-time snapshot across the dump duration.
metrics.remediation: Always use mongodump --oplog when backing up a replica set for consistency

metrics.description: A documented Recovery Point Objective. Without it, backup cadence and PITR retention have no benchmark to size against.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: A documented Recovery Time Objective. Without it, recovery procedures cannot be sized or rehearsed against a target.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Recency of the last successful restore drill. Untested restores frequently fail under real DR pressure.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular restore tests (at least quarterly)

metrics.description: A written disaster-recovery plan covering replica-set failover. Without one, recovery depends on individual operator memory.
metrics.remediation: Document disaster recovery procedures including replica failover and data restore runbooks

metrics.description: Whether backup retention satisfies organizational or regulatory policy. Required to prove recoverability over the mandated horizon.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup retention to meet compliance requirements (PBM retention policy or Atlas snapshot retention)

metrics.description: Whether oplog retention spans the gap between full backups. Required for PITR replay from the most recent restore point.
metrics.remediation: Ensure oplog retention period exceeds the time between backups to allow PITR

metrics.description: Existence of an offsite or cloud-object-storage backup copy. Required to survive site-level loss of the primary backup target.
metrics.remediation: Configure PBM to store backups in S3/GCS/Azure Blob or use Atlas Cloud Backup with multi-region

metrics.description: Whether server-side authentication (security.authorization) is on. Required to prevent unauthenticated access to all databases.
metrics.remediation: Enable authorization in mongod.conf: security.authorization: enabled

metrics.description: Whether SCRAM-SHA-256 is the active authentication mechanism. Older mechanisms (MONGODB-CR, SCRAM-SHA-1) are weaker and deprecated.
metrics.remediation: Ensure SCRAM-SHA-256 is in setParameter.authenticationMechanisms; upgrade users from MONGODB-CR

metrics.description: Whether the localhost exception has been closed by creating an admin user. While open, anyone with shell access can create privileged users.
metrics.remediation: Create an admin user in the admin database to disable the localhost exception

metrics.description: Use of x.509 certificate auth or LDAP for service/infrastructure accounts. Centralizes credential lifecycle outside the database.
metrics.remediation: Configure x.509 certificate authentication or LDAP for service accounts

metrics.description: Volume of failed authentication attempts over the last 24 hours. Spikes can indicate brute-force activity or misconfigured clients.
metrics.remediation: Investigate failed login sources in mongod log; consider IP allowlisting

metrics.description: Whether TLS/SSL is enforced on all client and inter-node connections (net.tls.mode). Required to prevent plaintext credentials and data on the wire.
metrics.remediation: Set net.tls.mode: requireTLS in mongod.conf and provide valid certificates

metrics.description: Minimum TLS protocol version negotiated. TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated and have known weaknesses.
metrics.remediation: Set net.tls.disabledProtocols: TLS1_0,TLS1_1 in mongod.conf

metrics.description: Whether data files are encrypted at rest via WiredTiger (Enterprise/KMIP) or disk-level encryption. Required to protect data on stolen or decommissioned media.
metrics.remediation: Enable WiredTiger encryption (Enterprise) with KMIP or use disk-level encryption (LUKS/AWS EBS)

metrics.description: External KMIP key management for encryption-at-rest. Enables key rotation and centralizes key lifecycle outside the database host.
metrics.remediation: Configure KMIP server in mongod.conf under security.kmip for external key management

metrics.description: Days of validity remaining on the active TLS certificate. Expiry causes immediate connection failures across the cluster.
metrics.remediation: Renew TLS certificate before expiration; configure certificate auto-rotation

metrics.description: Whether the audit log is on (Enterprise auditLog or equivalent). Required for security forensics and compliance evidence.
metrics.remediation: Enable audit log in mongod.conf under auditLog section (Enterprise) or configure syslog destination

metrics.description: Whether the audit filter captures authentication, authorization, and DDL events. A blank filter records nothing useful for security review.
metrics.remediation: Configure auditLog.filter to capture authenticate, createCollection, dropCollection, and createUser actions

metrics.description: Whether successful authorizations are also audited (auditAuthorizationSuccess). Required for full access traceability; has performance cost.
metrics.remediation: Set auditAuthorizationSuccess: true in mongod.conf (note: performance impact on high-throughput systems)

metrics.description: Server log verbosity (systemLog.verbosity). Too low loses connection/operation events; too high inflates log volume in production.
metrics.remediation: Set systemLog.verbosity: 1 for adequate logging; avoid verbosity > 2 in production

metrics.description: Days of mongod log history retained. Short retention prevents incident retrospectives and may breach compliance requirements.
metrics.remediation: Configure log rotation and retention policy (logrotate or Atlas log export) to retain logs for compliance period

metrics.description: Use of least-privilege role-based access control. Avoids handing out root or __system to accounts that don't need it.
metrics.remediation: Review user roles via db.getUsers(); assign least-privilege built-in roles or custom roles

metrics.description: Count of accounts holding the root or __system role. Excess super-users widen the blast radius of credential compromise.
metrics.remediation: Reduce root-role users to minimum; use readWrite, dbAdmin, or custom roles for application accounts

metrics.description: Whether custom roles avoid overly broad privilege combinations. Unbounded custom roles can effectively grant root by accident.
metrics.remediation: Review custom roles with db.getRoles({showPrivileges: true}); remove unnecessary privileges

metrics.description: Whether mongod's network binding (net.bindIp) excludes 0.0.0.0 or pairs it with firewalling. Open binding exposes the database to every reachable network.
metrics.remediation: Set net.bindIp in mongod.conf to specific interfaces; use firewall rules to restrict port 27017

metrics.description: Whether the Atlas IP access list limits connections to known CIDRs. A 0.0.0.0/0 entry exposes the cluster to the public internet.
metrics.remediation: Configure Atlas IP access list to specific CIDR ranges; avoid 0.0.0.0/0

metrics.description: Percentage of the WiredTiger cache currently in use. Sustained high usage drives eviction pressure and read latency.
metrics.remediation: Increase wiredTigerCacheSizeGB or add RAM; review working set size vs available memory

metrics.description: Ratio of data size to allocated disk capacity. Disks above 80% trend toward I/O slowdown and emergency cleanup work.
metrics.remediation: Expand storage, implement data archival, or enable sharding for horizontal scale-out

metrics.description: Effective WiredTiger compression ratio (uncompressed vs on-disk). Low ratios suggest compression is misconfigured or disabled.
metrics.remediation: Ensure WiredTiger snappy/zstd compression is enabled; verify blockCompressor in storage.wiredTiger.collectionConfig

metrics.description: Ratio of total index size to data size. Disproportionate indexes inflate memory pressure and write amplification.
metrics.remediation: Review and drop unused indexes; run db.collection.getIndexes() and analyze index usage stats

metrics.description: Active storage engine. WiredTiger is the only supported engine on modern MongoDB; legacy engines (MMAPv1) lack required durability features.
metrics.remediation: Migrate to WiredTiger storage engine; MMAPv1 is removed in MongoDB 4.0+

metrics.description: Live connections as a share of maxIncomingConnections. Approaching the cap leads to connection refusals and tail-latency spikes.
metrics.remediation: Increase maxIncomingConnections or implement connection pooling via mongos/proxy

metrics.description: Whether net.maxIncomingConnections is set explicitly. The default can let MongoDB exhaust OS file descriptors under load.
metrics.remediation: Set net.maxIncomingConnections in mongod.conf based on available OS file descriptors

metrics.description: Whether application drivers reuse pooled connections. Per-request connections cause socket exhaustion and TLS-handshake overhead.
metrics.remediation: Configure maxPoolSize/minPoolSize in the MongoDB driver connection string

metrics.description: Headroom of unused connection slots. Near-zero availability puts the cluster one client surge away from refused connections.
metrics.remediation: Increase maxIncomingConnections or reduce application connection pool sizes

metrics.description: Rate of page evictions falling onto application threads. Sustained pressure indicates undersized cache or working set overflow.
metrics.remediation: Increase WiredTiger cache size or add memory; investigate large document scans causing eviction pressure

metrics.description: Gap between dataSize and storageSize as a fragmentation proxy. Large gaps waste disk and may benefit from compact().
metrics.remediation: Run db.collection.compact() during maintenance window to reclaim fragmented space

metrics.description: Count of indexes with zero accesses since restart. Unused indexes consume memory and slow down writes for no benefit.
metrics.remediation: Drop unused indexes identified via $indexStats aggregation pipeline; reduces memory and write overhead

metrics.description: Whether TTL background deletes are running on time-series collections. Stalled TTL lets data grow past retention windows.
metrics.remediation: Verify TTL index background thread is running; check serverStatus().metrics.ttl for deletedDocuments activity

metrics.description: Share of the WiredTiger cache holding dirty pages. Above ~20%, aggressive eviction kicks in and write latency rises.
metrics.remediation: Increase checkpoint frequency (storage.syncPeriodSecs) or add memory to reduce dirty page buildup

metrics.description: Whether the oplog window covers planned maintenance durations. Too short forces full resyncs after taking secondaries offline.
metrics.remediation: Size oplog to cover at least 48h of write activity to handle planned maintenance

metrics.description: Whether the chunk balancer is on and not paused. Without it, hot shards accumulate and even distribution drifts.
metrics.remediation: Enable balancer: sh.startBalancer(); investigate if balancer was paused intentionally

metrics.description: Evenness of chunk counts across shards. Persistent imbalance signals shard-key skew or paused balancing.
metrics.remediation: Allow balancer to run; review shard key choice if chronic imbalance persists

metrics.description: Tracking of storage growth and a documented capacity plan. Without trend data, expansion happens reactively under pressure.
metrics.remediation: Implement storage monitoring with Ops Manager, Atlas, or Prometheus mongodb_exporter

metrics.description: Percentage of reads served from the WiredTiger cache. Low hit ratios push reads to disk and inflate latency.
metrics.remediation: Increase wiredTigerCacheSizeGB; ensure working set fits in cache; review large collection scans

metrics.description: Whether application threads are stalling to do page eviction. Any non-zero count means background eviction is falling behind.
metrics.remediation: Increase cache size or eviction worker threads (wiredTigerEngineRuntimeConfig: eviction=(threads_max=8))

metrics.description: Whether storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB is set explicitly. The 50%-of-RAM default ignores co-tenants and workload shape.
metrics.remediation: Set storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB explicitly in mongod.conf based on total RAM and workload

metrics.description: Headroom on WiredTiger read tickets. Exhaustion stalls reads until in-flight operations release tickets.
metrics.remediation: Investigate slow queries consuming tickets; consider increasing wiredTigerConcurrentReadTransactions if hardware allows

metrics.description: Headroom on WiredTiger write tickets. Exhaustion stalls writes and produces queue spikes under sustained load.
metrics.remediation: Investigate slow write operations; consider increasing wiredTigerConcurrentWriteTransactions

metrics.description: Whether the slow-query profiler is recording above slowms. Without it, expensive operations go unattributed and untunable.
metrics.remediation: Set profiling level 1 with appropriate slowms: db.setProfilingLevel(1, {slowms: 100})

metrics.description: Count of slow operations recorded in the last hour. Sustained high counts point to missing indexes or runaway queries.
metrics.remediation: Analyze slow query log (system.profile collection); add missing indexes or rewrite query plans

metrics.description: Recent queries hitting COLLSCAN in their explain plan. Full scans bypass indexes and scale linearly with collection size.
metrics.remediation: Create indexes to support query access patterns; use explain() to identify COLLSCAN queries

metrics.description: Share of reads served by an index. Low ratios indicate query patterns without supporting indexes.
metrics.remediation: Identify unindexed query patterns via profiler; create compound indexes for frequent query shapes

metrics.description: Ratio of scanned to returned documents on sharded queries. High ratios mean queries hit too many shards or scan too widely.
metrics.remediation: Include shard key in queries to enable targeted operations; review shard key selection

metrics.description: Profiler verbosity level. Level 2 logs every operation and degrades production write throughput; level 1 captures slow ops only.
metrics.remediation: Set profiler level to 1 (not 2); level 2 logs all operations causing significant overhead

metrics.description: Whether the query plan cache holds active entries. Empty caches force replanning and erase a key optimizer benefit.
metrics.remediation: Ensure indexes exist to allow plan caching; investigate plan cache evictions via planCacheListQueryShapes

metrics.description: Length of the global read/write lock queue. Sustained queueing indicates lock contention or long-running operations.
metrics.remediation: Investigate long-running operations via db.currentOp(); kill blocking operations if necessary

metrics.description: Count of currently active operations exceeding 30s runtime. Long ops often hold locks and starve other clients.
metrics.remediation: Use db.killOp(opId) for stuck operations; investigate root cause via explain() analysis

metrics.description: Count of operations waiting on WiredTiger tickets. Any wait indicates the engine is the bottleneck for concurrency.
metrics.remediation: Reduce concurrent operations or increase WiredTiger ticket counts; optimize slow queries

metrics.description: Round-trip time between application and MongoDB. High latency caps end-to-end throughput regardless of database tuning.
metrics.remediation: Co-locate application and MongoDB in same region/AZ; use read preferences appropriately

metrics.description: Replication lag of secondaries behind the primary. Excess lag risks stale reads and longer failover convergence.
metrics.remediation: Investigate secondary lag via rs.printSecondaryReplicationInfo(); check secondary hardware and network

metrics.description: Ratio of oplog window to current replication lag. Tight ratios mean a stalled secondary risks falling off the oplog.
metrics.remediation: Increase oplog size (replSetResizeOplog) to ensure replica can catch up after maintenance

metrics.description: Count of primary elections in the last 24h. Recurring elections indicate network instability, OOM kills, or disk stalls.
metrics.remediation: Investigate election cause in mongod logs; check for network partitions, OOM kills, or disk I/O stalls

metrics.description: Replica-set member states. Members stuck in RECOVERING, DOWN, or STARTUP reduce quorum margin and HA guarantees.
metrics.remediation: Investigate unhealthy members via rs.status(); check for RECOVERING, DOWN, or STARTUP states

metrics.description: Major.minor version against the supported GA window. Older lines (e.g. 6.0 EOL Jul 2025) drop out of security maintenance.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade to a supported MongoDB version; 5.0 EOL was October 2024, 4.4 EOL was February 2024

metrics.description: Whether the running build matches the latest patch for its major.minor line. Lagging patches accumulates known fixes and CVEs.
metrics.remediation: Apply latest patch via package manager; check https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/

metrics.description: Alignment of featureCompatibilityVersion (FCV) with the running binary. Stale FCV blocks new features and complicates upgrades.
metrics.remediation: Run db.adminCommand({setFeatureCompatibilityVersion: '<version>'}) to align FCV with actual version

metrics.description: Whether the running MongoDB version is still inside its support lifecycle. EOL versions receive no security patches.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade immediately; EOL versions receive no security patches. Refer to MongoDB lifecycle policy.

metrics.description: Compatibility of application drivers with the server version. Outdated drivers can break on server upgrade or miss new wire features.
metrics.remediation: Check driver compatibility matrix at https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/; upgrade drivers before server upgrade

metrics.description: Whether MongoDB runs as a replica set rather than standalone. Required for HA, online backups, and rolling maintenance.
metrics.remediation: Convert standalone to replica set: initiate rs.initiate() and add secondary members

metrics.description: Whether the replica set has an odd voter count. Even counts allow tied elections and degraded availability.
metrics.remediation: Add an arbiter or additional data-bearing member to achieve an odd number of voters

metrics.description: Reachability of mongos router instances. A failed mongos disconnects clients from the sharded cluster routing layer.
metrics.remediation: Restart failed mongos instances; investigate connectivity to config server replica set

metrics.description: Existence of a documented upgrade plan for the next major release. Without one, EOL deadlines arrive as emergencies.
metrics.remediation: Document upgrade path following MongoDB upgrade guide; plan FCV bump separately from binary upgrade

metrics.description: Use of deprecated MongoDB operators or commands in application code. Deprecated APIs can disappear in a future major release.
metrics.remediation: Review MongoDB release notes for deprecated operators; update queries to use current equivalents

metrics.description: Use of JSON Schema validators on collections. Without validation, malformed documents enter unchecked and harm downstream consumers.
metrics.remediation: Define JSON schema validators with db.runCommand({collMod: '<collection>', validator: {...}})

metrics.description: Use of the Change Streams API for event-driven integration. Direct oplog tailing is brittle and bypasses resume tokens.
metrics.remediation: Migrate from direct oplog tailing to Change Streams API for better abstraction and resilience

metrics.description: Whether a self-managed deployment has been assessed for Atlas migration. Surfaces blockers before a migration project commits.
metrics.remediation: Run MongoDB Atlas Assessment Tool (MAAT) to evaluate migration feasibility and effort

metrics.description: Use of mongodb+srv:// DNS seedlist URIs by clients. Hard-coded host lists prevent transparent topology changes.
metrics.remediation: Update connection strings to use mongodb+srv:// format to avoid hardcoded host lists

metrics.description: Whether MongoDB metrics flow into a monitoring backend (Atlas, Ops Manager, or Prometheus). Without it, incidents are detected by users.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Prometheus mongodb_exporter, Ops Manager agent, or enable Atlas monitoring integration

metrics.description: Whether alerts cover replication lag, disk usage, and connection count. Missing alerts let key failure modes go silent.
metrics.remediation: Configure alerts in Atlas, Ops Manager, or Prometheus Alertmanager for key MongoDB metrics

metrics.description: Profiler level chosen for production. Level 2 logs every operation and amplifies write cost; level 0/1 are safe defaults.
metrics.remediation: Disable level 2 profiling after debugging; profiling all ops causes significant write amplification

metrics.description: Presence of an Ops Manager or Cloud Manager agent. Provides centralized backup, monitoring, and automation for self-managed clusters.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Ops Manager or Cloud Manager agent for automated backup, monitoring, and deployment management

metrics.description: Total number of replica-set members. At least 3 are needed for safe quorum-based failover; an odd count avoids tied elections.
metrics.remediation: Deploy at least 3 replica set members for quorum-based failover

metrics.description: Availability of SCRAM-SHA-256 in the server's authentication mechanisms. Older mechanisms are weaker and should be phased out.
metrics.remediation: Enable SCRAM-SHA-256: net.tls.mode: requireTLS in mongod.conf

metrics.description: Total logical data size across databases. Tracked as input to capacity planning and growth analysis.
metrics.remediation: Monitor data size growth for capacity planning

metrics.description: Total collections across databases. Excessive proliferation can hint at multi-tenant or schema-per-tenant patterns.
metrics.remediation: Review collection proliferation for schema design issues

metrics.description: Total bytes of index storage. Used to compare against data size and to flag oversized index footprints.
metrics.remediation: Review index sizes relative to data size; consider removing unused indexes

metrics.description: Insert operations per second. Tracked as a baseline for write-volume capacity planning.
metrics.remediation: Monitor insert throughput for capacity planning

metrics.description: Query operations per second. Tracked as a baseline for read-volume and performance trend analysis.
metrics.remediation: Monitor query throughput for performance baselining

metrics.description: Update operations per second. Surfaces write-heavy workloads and write-amplification trends.
metrics.remediation: Monitor update throughput for write-heavy workloads

metrics.description: Delete operations per second. Persistent high rates may indicate churn or schema-design issues.
metrics.remediation: Monitor delete throughput; high delete rate may indicate schema design issues

metrics.description: Whether WiredTiger journaling is on. Required for durable crash recovery between checkpoints.
metrics.remediation: Enable journaling (default in WiredTiger)

metrics.description: Combined insert + update operations per second. Aggregate measure of write-side capacity demand.
metrics.remediation: Monitor write throughput for capacity baselining

metrics.description: Combined query + getmore operations per second. Aggregate measure of read-side capacity demand.
metrics.remediation: Monitor read throughput for performance baselining

metrics.description: Profiling level applied for slow-query capture. A non-zero level is needed to populate system.profile for tuning.
metrics.remediation: Set profiling level to 1 (slow queries only): db.setProfilingLevel(1, { slowms: 100 })

metrics.description: Whether any collection has a schema validator. Even partial coverage signals data-quality investment.
metrics.remediation: Add schema validation to key collections for data integrity
